The test image shows a tomato **stem** with an elongated, dark brown necrotic canker lesion running along the stem. The lesion has brownish-black necrotic center tissue with lighter/whitish margins, and the stem appears cracked/split. This is clearly a stem canker.

Top candidates: Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot, Southern_Blight.

Now I've used all 16 reference views. Let me make my final assessment.

**Summary of findings:**

- **Test image**: Close-up of a tomato stem at a node/junction showing an elongated, brown-dark necrotic canker with whitish/cream margins and cracked/split stem tissue. Rest of plant is green.

- **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**: All 3 references were microscopic spore images or a dry, detached stem — no useful macroscopic stem canker comparison.

- **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato**: Bugwood_5 showed stems with pale longitudinal streaks/lesions (close match to the elongated pattern); Bugwood_18 showed a stem close-up with a lighter streak and internal discoloration — both consistent with the test image's elongated stem canker with whitish margins.

- All other classes (late blight, anthracnose, TSWV, gray mold, early blight, etc.) showed leaf/fruit symptoms or wilt symptoms — none matched the stem canker in the test image.

The elongated, brown stem canker with whitish margins and longitudinal cracking is most consistent with **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato** (*Clavibacter michiganensis*), which classically produces this type of stem canker with pale margins on tomato stems.
